title: Book Two · Chapter 149: The Other Side of the Wall
story:
Late in the holiday, Ronan and Jun meet at the square. Leo is still away. Mei is visiting family for a few days. The two boys have one ball and enough shade beside the wall.

Jun takes a piece of chalk from his bag. He draws a little goal on the wall.

“Not the whole wall,” he says. “Only this square.”

Ronan kicks gently. The ball hits the top edge.

“In?”

“On the edge. Again.”

He tries again and reaches the middle. Jun gives him one point.

They take turns until Ronan has seven and Jun has eight. Ronan wants one more round. Jun agrees, then scores first.

“Nine,” he says.

“You were supposed to miss.”

“I forgot.”

Ronan laughs. His next ball goes wide. Jun gets it from the far side of the path.

When they sit down for water, Ronan asks about Jun's plans.

“Will you try for the reading places?”

“Probably not. The other activity fits my week better.”

“Are you sure?”

“Nearly. I will check all the times when school starts.”

Ronan nods. He thinks of Jun as a rival for a moment. If Jun does not try, Ronan may have a better chance. Then he feels ashamed of the thought.

“I will miss your questions,” he says instead.

Jun looks at him.

“You can hear them in the ordinary activity.”

“Right.”

For a while they watch a small child chase a ball. The child's father catches it before it reaches the road.

Ronan turns his bottle cap.

“Do you still think about the guide?”

“Sometimes.”

“Every time I answer?”

“No. But I remember when I need to trust an answer.”

Ronan presses the cap down.

“I do not want that to be the only thing.”

“It is not the only thing.”

Jun points at the chalk goal. “You also miss the middle.”

Ronan laughs, then rubs his face with his sleeve. It feels better and worse at the same time.

Jun stands. “One last round?”

They play five more turns. Ronan gets three clean goals. Jun gets two. They count only the goals from this last round.

At the end, they use a little water to wipe the chalk from the wall. The owner lets them draw there. But they must clean the wall afterwards.

Ronan carries the empty bottle. Jun carries the ball as far as the corner. There he gives it back.

“See you at school.”

“See you.”

Jun goes home. Ronan holds the ball under one arm. He is still sad about the guide. But he smiles as he remembers Jun's joke and their last game.
studyGuide:
## 词句提示

shade＝阴凉；rival＝竞争者；chalk＝粉笔；trust＝信任。

## 理解问题

1. Jun什么时候会想起旧小册子？
2. 他们怎样有边界地继续普通友谊？

## 读句子

**Jun / gives him / one point.** Jun／给他／记一分。
